summary: An exploratory negative-result essay, not a formalization: it asks whether embedding ZFC in Coq rescues a File Change Semantics mechanization, and answers 'partially, not enough'. Six modules: a Werner-style ZFC axiomatization (8 propositional axioms incl. choice) where files and info states are bare Ens and the CCP is a placeholder with body True; a Morse-Kelley variant whose unrestricted class-comprehension axiom the file itself proves Russell-inconsistent (class_comprehension_inconsistent, Qed — everything in that module is vacuous, as its own comment notes); a classical-ZFC module with an Admitted filter_exists; a stock-taking module with Admitted set_comprehension and an Admitted random_reset_not_unique that is false as written (its own comment concedes it needs Entity to have 2+ elements); a computation-vs-existence module whose only Qed is the trivial 'exists unit'; and a computable finite alternative (nat entities, list info states, CCP3 := InfoState3 -> list InfoState3, domain approximated by seq 0 10) that the file explicitly flags as 'a NEW theory, not a formalization of FCS'. The file's stated conclusion is that FCS cannot be fully mechanized without changing its fundamental character; its mechanized support for that claim is five Admitted proofs and one inconsistency finding.

evidence: No FCS construct receives a contentful definition: CCP_exists has body True, and all three CCP-operation Definitions end in Admitted, so no theorem in the file concerns Heim's objects (rubric §2 'unfaithful': theorems concern objects that are not the source's).
None of Heim's headline claims (novelty/familiarity, CCPs for connectives, truth via file change, projection, donkey conditionals) is even stated; the donkey 'theorem' is 'exists (sem : Type), True'.
Of the two Qed proofs, one is trivial and the other establishes that the file's own MK axiom pair is inconsistent — a finding about the encoding attempt, not about FCS.

8 propositional axioms (ZFC block + MK comprehension spec + omega_infinite) with the MK pair proven inconsistent in-file; 5 Admitted occurrences; random_reset_not_unique is false as written (missing 2+-element hypothesis its own comment names).
simplifications: ComputableAlternative: finite entity domain (seq 0 10), list info states, explicit list nondeterminism for random reset — but the file itself disclaims this as a new theory rather than a simplification of FCS
omissions: all of Heim's actual apparatus: file cards, novelty/familiarity conditions, felicity/definedness, CCPs for negation/conditionals/quantifiers, truth definition, the projection facts
additions: Werner-style ZFC axiomatization and MK class theory as substrates
the extended prose analysis of computation-vs-existence, type confusion, and attitude impredicativity (File_with_attitudes mutual inductive)

determination_rationale: The file's own verdict is 'cannot' ('FCS cannot be fully mechanized without changing its fundamental character'), but under rubric §4 that bar is not met by this file: the diagnosis rests on five Admitted proofs (one false as written), one of its two axiomatizations is proven inconsistent, and its central complaint — axiomatized sets don't compute — targets extraction/computability rather than mechanizability (Heim's CCPs on satisfaction sets are directly definable over Prop-level sets/Ensembles, which this file never attempts; 'we did not manage' is not 'cannot'). What the file does evidence is determination 3: the one working artifact recovers FCS-style existential update only after re-founding the theory (finite domains, explicit list nondeterminism for random reset, CCPs as InfoState -> list InfoState), a re-founding the file itself flags as changing the theory's commitments. It also correctly names two genuine pressure points a real formalization must face — random reset's nondeterminism (no canonical choice function) and the impredicativity of attitude-embedded info states — which are recorded here as the file's lasting contribution. A proper FCS record must come from a contentful formalization, not this probe.

artifact_classes.description: attitude impredicativity: files containing info states containing files — the file exhibits the File_with_attitudes / InfoState_with_attitudes mutual inductive and notes stratification is forced, losing quantification over all info states
type–value confusion diagnosed in prose: FCS conflates semantic_value (Prop) with context_update (Ens -> Ens), which Coq keeps as distinct types; also the MK set/class split
the file's central theme: axiomatized ZFC membership (IN) is opaque — comprehension/filtering/existential update are provable-existent but not computable; no extraction, no example-checking
IN x y undecidable even with LEM (the commented-out is_in : Ens -> bool); filter needs decidable predicates, which forces the bool-based finite alternative

notes: Record produced by the 2026-09-05 batch audit sweep; the file is a pre-atlas pilot predating the zero-axiom discipline (30 Parameter/Axiom declarations, 8 propositional, one axiom pair proven inconsistent in-file) and is best read as a design memo on why the atlas approach was needed, not as an atlas formalization of FCS.
